keyFindings.description: A notification the eviction interval refuses is dropped and nothing re-examines that room: there is no timer, no pending set, and recordEviction runs only after a successful Evict. So the trailing writes of a burst on the other process leave a connected reader holding text older than the stored head until that document is written again. staleRoomEvictInterval's own comment (:59-61) and run's (:122-124) both name roomIdleTimeout as the fallback, but service.go:44-47 defines it as the time a room stays resident after its last peer leaves - a room with a browser in it never goes idle, which the PR's own test note says in as many words (stale_room_eviction_test.go:95-96). The same hole covers every notification sent while the evictor's listener is redialling, since pglisten's OnConnected catch-up hook is nil in production for this evictor (stale_room.go:133, :97-100) and RedialBackoff reaches 30 s. No corruption: a write from such a room is refused and the room reloads; the damage is read-only staleness. It contradicts the PR body's bullet ('a write elsewhere closes that room within a notification round trip and the browser re-syncs') and the user documentation this PR adds (docs/site/src/content/docs/dispatch/running-dispatch.md:246-250: 'their browser reconnects, re-syncs and shows the current text'). Two acceptable answers: re-examine a refused room once the window elapses (a pending set plus one timer on the listener goroutine, which stays inside the interval's own rule of at most one eviction per room per interval), and give the evictor an OnConnected that re-examines its resident rooms; or, if the architect judges the gap acceptable, correct both code comments, the body bullet and running-dispatch.md to say a reader can hold text older than the stored head until that document is written again. Not caused by round 1's ordering fix: the refusal dropped the notification the same way when the interval was checked last.

reconcileDurableConsumer reads info.PushBound and then deletes and re-creates the durable in two separate round trips. A process that skipped the reconciliation - the lease is held elsewhere, or its throttle refused it - goes straight to client.Subscribe, and a Subscribe landing between the holder's ConsumerInfo and its DeleteConsumer binds a durable that is then deleted. Intake.Run has already called binds.Stop() once bound (intake.go:141), so nothing rebinds: that process's intake is idle for the life of the process with 'NATS consumer bound' as its last word. No message loss, since the deleting process creates the replacement and binds it, but the standby is silently gone. Narrow window and only on the one upgrade that meets a plural-filter durable from an earlier release; the PushBound guard is this diff's own, so the window is too. Re-read ConsumerInfo immediately before the delete, or restart the bind poll when a bound subscription reports its consumer deleted.

The claim pushes next_attempt_at out by claimWindow (60 s) for all 100 ids before any row is read, so when a row fails to scan and pgx kills the cursor, the claimed ids the batch never reached wait out the whole window. Before the claim they were re-selected on the next scan tick (retryInterval, 5 s). The comment states it deliberately; it is still a 12x latency regression on a path whose purpose is promptness, and claimWindow is sized for a healthy batch rather than for this case. Resetting next_attempt_at to null for the claimed ids this batch did not reach would close it.

The corrected lease-pool comment overshoots in one sentence: 'the next leased loop added here makes a ninth caller that waits for a connection rather than failing - the wait a standby's two-second bind poll takes anyway'. The same paragraph says a lease is held for the whole pass, minutes for the compaction, and that is what a ninth Acquire queues behind, not two seconds. Also left behind by this round: Listener's doc (pool.go:233) still names the delivery hub as the one holder, where three subsystems now dial through it (the hub, api/event_stream_relay.go, docs/stale_room.go), as pglisten/listener.go's own header already says.

Names the merge deleted, still in test prose: exclusive_test.go:217 pins const name = "delivery-consumers", a lease name that no longer exists now that consumerLease carries the durable, and its surrounding comment still describes one lease for 'the delivery consumers' reconciliation', which is now two; delivery/intake_test.go:67-68 names deliveryConsumerLease, an identifier commit 12183d35 removed. The quoted log lines in intake.go:363-365 keep the old name correctly, since they are a measurement.
